children: Spain's antitrust and energy watchdog CNMC said on Wednesday it was probing potential competition breaches in the country's energy markets.
The authority said in a statement it had been looking into potential infractions amounting to abuse of a dominant position.
In particular, the CNMC is focusing on possible discriminatory practices limiting the ability of third-party operators to access and compete on the Spanish energy market.

Between October 26-29, the watchdog raided the headquarters of an unnamed group operating in the energy sector. The CNMC declined to comment on the name of the targeted company or provide further details.
Such inspections are a preliminary step in an investigation and do not imply that the target will be found guilty.
Should the authority confirm such practices, they would be a serious infringement of competition rules, it said, carrying a potential fine of up to 10% of a company's revenue.
